narrative:
The model determined that you have a 36% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and your installment rate as a percentage of income. Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the single most influential piece of information. This history pushed the prediction toward approval because it signals that you have successfully managed past obligations. However, this positive influence was outweighed by two other factors.

The status of your checking account, which shows it is currently in negative balance (<0 DM), was the second most important driver and worked strongly against you. Only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in this range, so the model viewed this as a clear warning sign of financial strain. Your requested installment rate of 2% of disposable income, while lower than the 3% average among approved loans, still pulled the prediction slightly toward denial, likely because the overall loan size of 5,302 DM is substantially higher than the 3,020 DM average for successful applications.

Taken together, these signals led the bank to decline the request. To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account balance into positive territory, reduce the loan amount you are requesting, and consider waiting until your credit history shows even more consistent on-time payments. You may wish to reapply once these areas have improved. (248 words)
